overall_summary: The Orders API is a small NestJS 10 service (Auth, Users, Orders modules on TypeORM/PostgreSQL) that debits a user's balance when an order is placed. Module structure is clean and controllers are mostly thin, but the service is not safe to expose. Authentication can be forged (SEC-002), an unauthenticated endpoint is SQL-injectable (SEC-004), clients choose their own prices (SEC-003), and production credentials are committed in three places (SEC-001, SEC-005, OPS-001, OPS-002). The money path (placeOrder) has no transaction, no locking and no tests (API-002, TEST-002).
health_assessment: The rating is driven by four confirmed Critical security defects that are each exploitable without credentials, plus fourteen High findings concentrated in the order/balance flow and the deployment setup. The codebase is small and conventionally structured, so most fixes are local: verify JWTs, parameterize one query, validate DTOs, wrap placeOrder in a transaction, and move secrets to configuration.
architecture_overview: Three feature modules (`auth`, `users`, `orders`) follow Nest conventions, each with its own module, controller and service, plus TypeORM entities. Requests flow controller → service → TypeORM repository. `AuthModule` depends one-way on `UsersModule`. `UsersModule` and `OrdersModule` depend on each other through `forwardRef` (ARC-004) because `UsersService.getProfileWithOrders` composes order data. Business rules leak into `OrdersController` (discount and validation, ARC-002), and the balance debit is implemented in `OrdersService` against another module's entity (ARC-003). Token issuing and verification are split between `AuthService` and a free-standing `JwtGuard` that shares no configuration (ARC-001).
dependency_analysis:
`scripts/import-graph.py` found 27 internal import edges and three cycles:

- `src/orders/orders.service.ts` ↔ `src/users/users.service.ts`: a real design cycle (ARC-004)
- `src/orders/orders.module.ts` ↔ `src/users/users.module.ts`: the module-level mirror of the same cycle, papered over with `forwardRef` (ARC-004)
- `src/orders/order.entity.ts` ↔ `src/users/user.entity.ts`: the standard TypeORM bidirectional relation with lazy types, which is benign

Removing `getProfileWithOrders` from `UsersService` makes the dependency one-way (Orders → Users) and removes both `forwardRef`s.
security_overview: Authentication is a hand-written `JwtGuard` that only *decodes* tokens (SEC-002), applied to a single route (POST /orders). Every read endpoint is public, with no ownership checks (SEC-007), and returns full entities including password hashes (SEC-008), which are unsalted MD5 (SEC-006). The only raw SQL in the codebase is injectable and reachable anonymously (SEC-004). Order totals come from client-supplied prices, so a negative price credits the balance (SEC-003). Secrets: the database password is in `app.module.ts` and `.env` (SEC-001, OPS-001) and the JWT signing key is in `auth.service.ts` and the Dockerfile (SEC-005, OPS-002). Rotate all of them; moving them is not enough.

owasp_notes.A01: No guards or ownership checks on read endpoints; full entities exposed
owasp_notes.A02: Unsalted MD5 password hashing; hard-coded signing key
owasp_notes.A03: Raw SQL template string in UsersService.search
owasp_notes.A04: Client-controlled prices in the money path
owasp_notes.A05: Secrets in .env and image ENV; permissive CORS; no helmet
owasp_notes.A06: Not assessed online (no network authorization); no lockfile committed (OPS-006)
owasp_notes.A07: Signature never verified; tokens never expire; no login throttling
owasp_notes.A08: No deserialization or unsigned-webhook surface found
owasp_notes.A09: Failures in POST /orders are swallowed with no logging (API-001)

strategic_recommendations.title: Make authentication real, then apply it by default
strategic_recommendations.detail: Replace the hand-written guard with @nestjs/jwt (`JwtService.verifyAsync`) configured once in AuthModule from ConfigService, register it as a global `APP_GUARD` with an `@Public()` decorator for login, and add ownership checks in the services.

strategic_recommendations.title: Make placeOrder a single, server-priced transaction
strategic_recommendations.detail: Accept only `{ sku, quantity }` through a validated DTO, price items server-side, and perform the conditional debit, the order insert and a bulk item insert inside one `dataSource.transaction`, keyed by an idempotency key. Then cover it with unit and e2e tests.

strategic_recommendations.title: Move every secret and setting into validated configuration
strategic_recommendations.detail: Adopt @nestjs/config with a schema that requires DB_* and JWT_SECRET, use `TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync`, delete `.env` and the Dockerfile ENV, add `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` and `.env.example`, and rotate the exposed credentials.

strategic_recommendations.title: Switch schema management to migrations and fix the money types
strategic_recommendations.detail: Turn off `synchronize`, generate a baseline migration, then migrate money columns to `numeric(12,2)` or integer cents and add constraints (unique email, FK on order items, non-negative balance, indexes).

strategic_recommendations.title: Turn CI into a real gate
strategic_recommendations.detail: Commit a lockfile, add @nestjs/cli, fix the Jest config, run `npm ci`, tests and `npm audit` on pull requests, and pin actions and the Node image to the same LTS.

positive_observations: Clear module boundaries: each feature folder has its own module, controller, service and entity
UsersController and AuthController are thin and follow the README's layering convention
Constructor injection is used consistently, with no field injection
Login returns one generic error for unknown email and wrong password, so it does not enable user enumeration
Repository lookups outside UsersService.search use parameterized TypeORM where clauses
limitations: Static review only: no code was executed, built or tested, and no coverage figures are claimed
Dependency vulnerabilities were not checked online (no network authorization); OPS-004 recommends `npm audit` in CI

In this validation run the reviewer agents had only the Read tool available (Grep/Glob were not provided by the host), so they located files by path; all 22 repository files were read by at least one agent
25 same-location pairs reported by different agents were reviewed by the orchestrator and kept separate as distinct issues; 4 true duplicates were merged (see validation notes)
